title: Hop-level routing decision attribution stream & compact traces
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Current routing telemetry emits coarse ‘final decision’ events and scattered per-hop logs. This makes it hard to attribute latency/cost/quality regressions to a specific routing hop (region selection, tier route, or fallback model variant) and to compute per-hop SLOs. We need a compact, consistent event stream and trace shape that represents each routing decision as a sequence of hops with attribution metadata and delta-encoded metrics.

Goals:
- Produce a compact hop-level attribution event for every routed request that captures: requested model, candidate variants considered, selection reason, per-hop latencies, token counts, fallbacks triggered, and routing policy id.
- Emit a lightweight, optional compact span/trace that can be sampled and attached to distributed traces for debugging.
- Add derived per-hop metrics (p95 latency, error-rate, cost-per-token) with labels for region, tier, model_variant, and policy.
- Keep overhead low: target telemetry payload < 1 KB when sampling off; enable richer payloads when sampling on.
- Support privacy: strip customer prompt content and offer PII-safe mode.

Proposal (high level):
1) New telemetry event type: route_attribution.v1 — a compact JSON/protobuf message encoded with the following top-level fields: request_id, timestamp, route_policy_id, candidate_list (ids and variant reasons), selected_hop_index, hops (delta-encoded list with latency_ms, tokens_generated, backend_model_id, region, tier, fallback_flag), decision_trace_id (for correlating sampled full traces), sampling_level.
2) Emit route_attribution.v1 into the existing telemetry bus (kafka topic telemetry.route_attribution) before and after routing decisions so both pre-decision and post-decision snapshots are available.
3) Implement delta-encoding for hops to avoid repeating global fields; run a short LZ4 compression in the router for bursty requests to keep payload small.
4) A parallel compact trace span (op=route.decision.compact) will be created when sampling_level >= DEBUG. That span contains a short protobuf reference to the full decision trace stored in the trace-blob store (for on-demand fetch in debugging sessions).
5) Aggregation: a stream processor (Flink/Materialize) materializes per-hop time series and a per-policy rollup used by Console dashboards and alerting.
6) Rollout: feature-flagged by customer tier and region, default off for low-tier customers; gradually enable sampled attribution for 10% of requests in Canary, then 50%, then all for internal teams.

Data retention & cost controls:
- Raw route_attribution events: 30 days for sampled=DEBUG, 7 days otherwise.
- Materialized per-hop metrics: 13 months.
- Provide opt-out and PII-safe mode (customer-managed flag) that redacts request metadata and shortens retention.

Telemetry budget and perf constraints:
- Router CPU budget for telemetry: <1% p99 increase in request latency. Microbenchmarks show json + lz4 adds ~0.6ms median on the critical path when sampling on; when sampling off we emit a delta-only record to the async telemetry writer with <0.2ms overhead.

Acceptance criteria (summary):
- route_attribution.v1 events emitted for 95% of routed requests in the Canary cohort with payload <1.2KB median.
- Console dashboard shows per-hop p95 latencies and error rates within +/-5% of raw request traces.
- Debugging flow: given a sampled request_id, engineers can fetch full decision trace and see hop attribution within <10s.
- Feature flagging works per-customer and per-region.

- Proto schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/2156
- Stream processor PoC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/tree/main/route-attribution-poc
- Dashboard (draft): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/route-attribution/route-attribution-overview
